title: Where is the robot?
summary: Pose estimation, and why it drifts from the truth.

say.never: A **pose** is a robot's position on the field (x and y) *and* which way it's facing. The pose estimator works it out by adding up every tiny movement of the wheels, like counting your steps to guess how far you walked.
say.bit: A **pose** is where the robot is (x, y) and which way it faces. The pose estimator adds up every small wheel movement.

say.never: Your code only works once it's started. Press **Start** and wait until the status says **Running**.
say.bit: Your code only runs once it's built and started.

hint.never: press Start, then wait for Running.
hint.bit: press Start and wait for Running.

say.never: Choose **Teleop**, then press **Enable**. The robot stays frozen until it's enabled.
say.bit: Pick **Teleop** and press **Enable**. Robot code runs only while it's enabled.

say.never: Open **AdvantageScope** and click the **2D Field** tab. It's a map of the field from above.
say.bit: Open the 2D Field tab in AdvantageScope.

say.never: Type `Pose` in the search box. Drag **Drive/Pose** onto the **Poses** area. A little robot appears on the map. That's where *your code thinks* the robot is.
Now drag **Drive/TruePose** on too. The simulator secretly knows where the robot *really* is, so you can compare your guess to the truth.
say.bit: Now drag **Drive/TruePose** on too. The simulator knows where the robot **really** is.

say.never: Drive a long way. The two robots start together but slowly drift apart. Wheels slip a tiny bit and sensors are never perfect, so the guess gets worse over time. Real robots fix this with cameras and a gyro.
say.bit: Drive a long way. The two robots start together and slowly drift apart: wheels slip and encoders are never perfect. Real robots add cameras and gyros to correct it.
